output.methodChoice: D (competing hypotheses) with careful reasoning: several rival explanations, and the key question is whether the rise is real.
output.brief:
Store 14's rising shrink is not yet shown to be a real rise in losses. The Q1–Q3 figures are extrapolated estimates with an error of about ±0.6 points a quarter. Across the chain, about half of the stores that showed two straight rises like this were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's full-count shrink has been 1.5–1.8% for three years. The rise in logged shoplifting incidents matches a chain-wide jump after the incident app launched on 1 April, while chain shrink stayed flat. So it doesn't show more theft. The sales mix hasn't changed, so that explanation is out. The ethics-line tip was checked against CCTV and found to show only cardboard bale runs. Self-checkout, the bus interchange footfall and staff theft are all unproven.

What to do: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and refuse Regional Operations' proposal to drop it, because dropping it would remove the only reliable measurement. Hold off on a guard, pulling the self-checkout lanes, or any action against the night stocker until the count result is compared with the interim figures. Then target action at whatever the count shows. Confidence is moderate to good. The main uncertainty is whether a real rise exists at all.
